source_metadata.title: Effects on Blood Pressure of Reduced Dietary Sodium and the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) Diet

atoms.canonical_statement: The DASH-Sodium trial evaluated how three dietary sodium levels, the DASH dietary pattern, and their combination affect blood pressure in adults with and without hypertension.

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: The study was a multicenter randomized feeding trial conducted from September 1997 through November 1999 at four clinical centers, with parallel assignment to DASH or control diet and crossover exposure to sodium levels within the assigned diet.

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligibility required age at least 22 years, mean screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg, and mean diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg; major exclusions included heart disease, renal insufficiency, poorly controlled hyperlipidemia or diabetes, insulin-requiring diabetes, special dietary requirements, more than 14 alcoholic drinks weekly, and medications affecting blood pressure or nutrient metabolism.

population.label: Eligible DASH-Sodium trial participants
inclusion_criteria: Mean systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg
Mean diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg
exclusion_criteria: Poorly controlled hyperlipidemia or diabetes mellitus
More than 14 alcoholic drinks per week
Use of antihypertensive drugs or other medications affecting blood pressure or nutrient metabolism

atoms.canonical_statement: A total of 412 participants were randomized: 208 to the DASH diet and 204 to the control diet; 41% of each diet group had hypertension, 56-57% were Black, and 54-59% were women.

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: The DASH diet emphasized fruits, vegetables, low-fat dairy foods, whole grains, poultry, fish, and nuts; limited red meat, sweets, and sugar-containing beverages; and contained less total and saturated fat and cholesterol and more potassium, calcium, magnesium, fiber, and protein than the control diet.

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

exposures.details: Controlled feeding pattern emphasizing fruits, vegetables, low-fat dairy, whole grains, poultry, fish, and nuts; reduced red meat, sweets, sugar-containing beverages, total fat, saturated fat, and cholesterol.

atoms.canonical_statement: The control diet was designed to be typical of what many people in the United States eat.

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

concept.text: Control diet typical of U.S. intake

atoms.canonical_statement: At an energy intake of 2100 kcal, the sodium targets were 150 mmol/day (high), 100 mmol/day (intermediate), and 50 mmol/day (low), with sodium scaled proportionally to individual energy requirements.

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: Participants were provided all foods, including snacks and cooked meals; nutrient composition was monitored with chemical analysis, diets were taste-tested, and energy intake was adjusted to maintain body weight.

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: After a two-week run-in on the high-sodium control diet, participants were randomized to DASH or control diet and then consumed high, intermediate, and low sodium levels for 30 consecutive days each in random order.

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary outcome was systolic blood pressure at the end of each 30-day dietary intervention period, and the secondary outcome was diastolic blood pressure.

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

outcome.definition: Primary: systolic blood pressure at the end of each 30-day period; secondary: diastolic blood pressure.
outcome.measurement_method: Clinic sphygmomanometer measurements averaged over the last five measurements of each intervention period

atoms.canonical_statement: Blood pressure was measured with random-zero sphygmomanometers at repeated visits; participants and dietary staff were unaware of outcome data, and personnel collecting outcome data were unaware of diet assignment.

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: Dietary adherence was assessed using daily food diaries, on-site weekday meals, and 24-hour urinary excretion of sodium, potassium, phosphorus, and urea nitrogen.

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: Primary analyses used a generalized-estimating-equation model accounting for within-person repeated blood-pressure measurements, with baseline blood pressure, clinical center, cohort, intervention period, and carryover terms; protocol-specified subgroup interactions were examined and Holm adjustment was used for multiple comparisons.

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: Analyses followed the intention-to-treat approach; in 22 instances of missing blood-pressure measurements during an intervention period, baseline values were substituted.

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: The planned sample size of 400 provided 90% power to detect a 2.1-mm Hg systolic blood-pressure difference between sodium levels and a 3.0-mm Hg difference between DASH and control diets at each sodium level.

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: Completion of all intervention periods with blood-pressure measurements was 95% in the DASH group (198/208) and 94% in the control group (192/204).

concept.text: Completion of all intervention periods with blood-pressure measurements

atoms.canonical_statement: Mean 24-hour urinary sodium excretion during the high sodium period was approximately 142 mmol/day overall; values were 144 mmol/day on DASH and 141 mmol/day on the control diet.

Intermediate sodium level on control diet

atoms.canonical_statement: Mean 24-hour urinary sodium excretion during the low sodium period was approximately 65 mmol/day overall; values were 67 mmol/day on DASH and 64 mmol/day on the control diet.

atoms.canonical_statement: Urinary potassium, phosphorus, and urea nitrogen were higher with the DASH diet than with the control diet and were nearly identical across sodium levels within each assigned diet; body weight remained stable as intended.

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: On the control diet, reducing sodium from the high to the intermediate level lowered systolic blood pressure by 2.1 mm Hg (95% CI, 0.8 to 3.4 mm Hg lower; P<0.001).

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: On the control diet, reducing sodium from the intermediate to the low level produced an additional 4.6-mm Hg reduction in systolic blood pressure (95% CI, 3.2 to 5.9 mm Hg lower; P<0.001).

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: On the DASH diet, reducing sodium from the high to the intermediate level lowered systolic blood pressure by 1.3 mm Hg (95% CI, 0.0 to 2.6 mm Hg lower; P=0.03).

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: On the DASH diet, reducing sodium from the intermediate to the low level produced an additional 1.7-mm Hg reduction in systolic blood pressure (95% CI, 0.4 to 3.0 mm Hg lower; P<0.01).

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: On the control diet, high-to-low sodium reduction lowered systolic blood pressure by 6.7 mm Hg (95% CI, 5.4 to 8.0 mm Hg lower; P<0.001).

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: On the DASH diet, high-to-low sodium reduction lowered systolic blood pressure by 3.0 mm Hg (95% CI, 1.7 to 4.3 mm Hg lower; P<0.001).

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: At the high sodium level, systolic blood pressure was 5.9 mm Hg lower with DASH than with the control diet (95% CI, 3.7 to 8.0 mm Hg lower; P<0.001).

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: At the intermediate sodium level, systolic blood pressure was 5.0 mm Hg lower with DASH than with the control diet (95% CI, 2.5 to 7.6 mm Hg lower; P<0.001).

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: At the low sodium level, systolic blood pressure was 2.2 mm Hg lower with DASH than with the control diet (95% CI, 0.1 to 4.4 mm Hg lower; P<0.05).

atoms.canonical_statement: Compared with the high-sodium control diet, the low-sodium DASH diet lowered systolic blood pressure by 8.9 mm Hg (95% CI, 6.7 to 11.1 mm Hg lower; P<0.001).

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: On the control diet, high-to-low sodium reduction lowered diastolic blood pressure by 3.5 mm Hg (95% CI, 2.6 to 4.3 mm Hg lower; P<0.001).

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: On the DASH diet, high-to-low sodium reduction lowered diastolic blood pressure by 1.6 mm Hg (95% CI, 0.8 to 2.5 mm Hg lower; P<0.001).

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: Compared with the high-sodium control diet, the low-sodium DASH diet lowered diastolic blood pressure by 4.5 mm Hg (95% CI, 3.1 to 5.9 mm Hg lower; P<0.001).

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: Dietary sodium had approximately twice as large an effect on blood pressure during the control diet as during the DASH diet (interaction P<0.001).

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: Within the control diet, the approximately 40-mmol/day sodium reduction from intermediate to low sodium lowered blood pressure more than the similar reduction from high to intermediate sodium (P=0.03 for systolic and P=0.045 for diastolic blood pressure).

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: The DASH diet lowered systolic blood pressure at every sodium level and lowered diastolic blood pressure at the high and intermediate sodium levels; its blood-pressure effect was larger at high than at low sodium (interaction P<0.001).

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: The low-sodium DASH combination lowered systolic and diastolic blood pressure more than either DASH alone or sodium reduction alone, but the combined effect was smaller than strict additivity would predict (interaction P<0.001).

population.label: Adults in the DASH-Sodium trial with screening systolic blood pressure 120-159 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure 80-95 mm Hg

atoms.canonical_statement: Compared with the high-sodium control diet, the low-sodium DASH diet lowered systolic blood pressure by 11.5 mm Hg in participants with hypertension (P<0.001).

atoms.canonical_statement: Compared with the high-sodium control diet, the low-sodium DASH diet lowered systolic blood pressure by 7.1 mm Hg in participants without hypertension (P<0.001).

atoms.canonical_statement: Compared with the high-sodium control diet, the low-sodium DASH diet lowered systolic blood pressure by 6.8 mm Hg in men (P<0.001).

atoms.canonical_statement: The sodium effect was greater in participants with hypertension than in those without hypertension (interaction P=0.01 on the control diet and P=0.003 on the DASH diet).

atoms.canonical_statement: On the control diet, the sodium effect was greater in Black participants than in participants of other races or ethnic groups (interaction P=0.007).

atoms.canonical_statement: On the DASH diet, the sodium effect was greater in women than in men (interaction P=0.04).

atoms.canonical_statement: A transient systolic blood pressure above 170 mm Hg or diastolic blood pressure above 105 mm Hg occurred in 36 participants assigned to the control diet and 7 assigned to DASH; none occurred during the low-sodium DASH phase, and no participant reached the predefined threshold for sustained elevation requiring referral for antihypertensive therapy.

atoms.canonical_statement: Headache was reported at least once by 47% of participants during the high-sodium control phase, 39% during the low-sodium control phase, and 36% during the low-sodium DASH phase; both low-sodium comparisons with high-sodium control were significant at P<0.05.

atoms.canonical_statement: The number of participants not completing an intervention period was similar across the high-, intermediate-, and low-sodium periods (7, 7, and 8 participants, respectively).

atoms.canonical_statement: The intervention periods were brief, lasting only 30 days each.

atoms.canonical_statement: Long-term health benefits were not demonstrated and were stated to depend on whether people can sustain dietary changes and on increased availability of lower-sodium foods.

atoms.canonical_statement: The trial was supported by cooperative agreements and grants from the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute and by the General Clinical Research Center Program of the National Center for Research Resources; multiple food companies and organizations donated food.

The authors concluded that lowering sodium intake below the then-recommended 100 mmol/day level and following the DASH diet each substantially lower blood pressure, with the greatest effect when combined, supporting a more aggressive sodium-reduction target together with the DASH diet for prevention and treatment of elevated blood pressure.
